headline: PM Tareq Rahman to visit New York for UNGA 81st session on Monday
summary: The Prime Minister will deliver a speech on September 24 and hold high-level meetings with global leaders, including US President Donald Trump.
details: Prime Minister Tareq Rahman is traveling to New York this coming Monday, September 21, to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). He is scheduled to deliver a speech at the assembly on September 24.
According to Ministry of Foreign Affairs sources, the visit has been shortened. The Prime Minister will depart New York for Dhaka on the night of September 25, following his address to the assembly.

Initially, the visit was planned from September 21 to 29, with preparations being made for a trip to San Francisco. However, the itinerary has been reduced to a shorter, more austere visit with a smaller delegation than previous governments.

While in New York, the Prime Minister will participate in high-level UN meetings on development, pandemic prevention, sea-level rise, and nuclear disarmament. Bangladesh will also organize several discussions, including one on the Rohingya crisis.
Diplomatic sources indicate that bilateral meetings are being prepared with leaders from Pakistan, Kuwait, Canada, Thailand, Bhutan, Croatia, and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister.

Additionally, the Prime Minister is set to meet with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, the President of the European Council, the World Bank President, and the President of Boeing Global.
The Prime Minister will also attend a dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump.
caption:
PM Tareq Rahman heads to New York for the 81st UNGA session. A shortened, austere visit with a high-impact agenda.

Prime Minister Tareq Rahman is traveling to New York this coming Monday, September 21, to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). He is scheduled to deliver a speech at the assembly on September 24.

According to Ministry of Foreign Affairs sources, the visit has been shortened. The Prime Minister will depart New York for Dhaka on the night of September 25, following his address to the assembly.

Initially, the visit was planned from September 21 to 29, with preparations being made for a trip to San Francisco. However, the itinerary has been reduced to a shorter, more austere visit with a smaller delegation than previous governments.

While in New York, the Prime Minister will participate in high-level UN meetings on development, pandemic prevention, sea-level rise, and nuclear disarmament. Bangladesh will also organize several discussions, including one on the Rohingya crisis.

Diplomatic sources indicate that bilateral meetings are being prepared with leaders from Pakistan, Kuwait, Canada, Thailand, Bhutan, Croatia, and Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister.

Additionally, the Prime Minister is set to meet with UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, the President of the European Council, the World Bank President, and the President of Boeing Global.

The Prime Minister will also attend a dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump.

headline_marked: PM Modi [[thanks Tarique Rahman for birthday wishes]]
headline: PM Modi thanks Tarique Rahman for birthday wishes
summary: The Indian Prime Minister expressed his appreciation for the warm greetings sent by the Bangladesh Prime Minister on his birthday.
details: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanked Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for his birthday greetings in a post on X.
Modi wrote, "Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words."
The message of gratitude was shared by the High Commission of India in Bangladesh on its official Facebook page.
Earlier, the Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh extended birthday wishes to Modi via a Facebook post, including a greeting card.
The greeting message wished the Indian leader good health, high spirits, and continued dedicated service to the people of India.
caption:
A gesture of diplomatic courtesy: PM Narendra Modi thanks PM Tarique Rahman for birthday greetings.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi thanked Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman for his birthday greetings in a post on X.

Modi wrote, "Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words."

The message of gratitude was shared by the High Commission of India in Bangladesh on its official Facebook page.

Earlier, the Prime Minister's Office of Bangladesh extended birthday wishes to Modi via a Facebook post, including a greeting card.

The greeting message wished the Indian leader good health, high spirits, and continued dedicated service to the people of India.
